Subject: Question: DPA incident timelines and evidence exports

Jonas,

Thanks for the quick onboarding call earlier. As we're finalizing the DPA, Legal flagged a few items we need to confirm about incident notification and cross-border evidence access before we proceed:

- Are you able to commit to a 72-hour initial notification window for incidents affecting OptiBank data, including an initial assessment of scope and affected records? Our regulator expects that as a baseline.
- What information will be included in that initial notice (scope, affected data elements, severity category, immediate mitigations)?
- For forensic evidence exports (memory snapshots, telemetry, logs), can Redwood export to an OptiBank-controlled S3 bucket in eu-west-1 or do you require us to accept evidence in a Redwood-managed bucket?
- Who is the operational liaison on your side for expedited evidence requests (names/roles and escalation path)?

We prefer explicit wording around subprocessors: specifically, OptiBank needs confirmation that Redwood will notify us if a subprocessor is implicated and provide a plan for evidence collection from that subprocessor.

Can you confirm these items or point us to the appropriate contacts? If you prefer, send a short staged-notify proposal and we'll iterate.

Thanks,
Maya Shah
Senior Counsel, OptiBank

Maya — thanks, good questions. Looping in Legal (Kimberly) and Ops (Marissa, Ben) to confirm the exact language and operational feasibility. High level:

- Notification windows: we generally operate on a staged notification pattern: immediate acknowledgement on discovery, a preliminary assessment within 24-72 hours, and a formal incident notice with investigation summary within our agreed notification window. We can accept 72 hours as the formal notification SLA for reportable incidents, subject to limited carve-outs (e.g., ongoing criminal investigations or subprocessors requiring mutual legal steps).
- Initial notice contents: we typically include incident category, affected services, estimated scope (number of affected accounts or records when known), immediate mitigations, and next steps. We will not include raw PII in initial notices.
- Evidence exports: operationally we can export artifacts, but cross-border transfers depend on the artifact type and applicable export controls. Kimberly — please advise on the contractual angle. Marissa/Ben — can you confirm whether we can push encrypted forensic bundles to an OptiBank S3 in eu-west-1 under a short-term pre-signed URL or whether we prefer Redwood-managed transfer?

I'll draft a short staged-notify proposal and circulate once we have legal sign-off.

—Jonas

Team / Maya — quick legal position to inform ops:

- Contractual notification: Redwood can accept a 72-hour formal notification window for incidents that meet the "reportable incident" definition in the DPA (unauthorized access, exfiltration, irreversible data loss). We will provide an initial contact/acknowledgement as soon as we discover or are notified. We need to preserve exceptions for criminal subpoenas, government gag orders, and where immediate disclosure would impede an ongoing criminal investigation.

- Notice contents: confirmable items should include nature of incident, services impacted, estimated timeframe, preliminary scope (categories of data and estimated record counts), immediate remedial actions, and a point of contact. We will not include raw PII or forensic images in the notice body.

- Subprocessors: Redwood will notify OptiBank within the same notification window if a subprocessor is implicated and provide the subprocessor name, role, and planned actions. For evidence collection from a subprocessor we will coordinate the request; in many cases the subprocessor requires the customer or Redwood to initiate the request depending on data flows and contractual rights.

- Cross-border evidence export: we can provide evidence exports but need either (a) explicit customer instruction and acceptance of transfer (OptiBank signs an export waiver for specific artifacts), or (b) a formal legal process if the subprocessor's hosting jurisdiction prohibits direct transfer. We can also produce encrypted forensic bundles to an OptiBank-controlled bucket (pre-signed, limited TTL) provided the customer accepts appropriate controls and written instruction.

Operational asks: can Ops confirm time-to-produce for a standard forensic snapshot (logs + KV cache export + system metadata) and whether we can automate a pre-signed S3 delivery to eu-west-1? If evidence requires extended processing or vendor cooperation, we need to call out potential delays in the DPA.

I've attached a first-pass set of redlines for the incident-notify clause (Draft_DPA_redlines_OptiBank_v1.docx) and a checklist of artifacts we can typically produce (Export_Checklist.csv). Ops, please review and call out any items that are not feasible within the proposed windows.

Maya — thanks for the patience. Ops read-through and proposed operational commitments below (based on Kimberly's redlines). Happy to fold this into the DPA redline doc and send to you as a clean track-change when we have agreement.

Proposed staged-notify and evidence delivery commitments (operational summary):

1) Discovery acknowledgement: within 6 hours of detection or notification we will send an acknowledgement with the assigned incident ID and a primary contact.

2) Preliminary assessment: within 24-72 hours we will provide a high-level assessment with incident category, estimated scope (buckets: accounts affected / records impacted estimate), immediate mitigations, and next steps. If the assessment requires more time because of vendor/subprocessor coordination, we'll flag that in the acknowledgement.

3) Formal incident notice: within 72 hours if the event meets reportable criteria; includes finalized assessment or a statement of outstanding items and ETA for full report.

4) Evidence exports: we can deliver the following options depending on artifact type: (a) encrypted forensic bundles to an OptiBank pre-signed S3 location in eu-west-1 (48h TTL on pre-signed URLs), (b) secure transfer to a Redwood-managed transfer bucket with mutual access, or (c) in exceptional cases, provide access via a joint forensics session. Some artifacts (raw memory snapshots, certain telemetry) may require extended processing (7-14 days) to sanitize and package; we will flag those in the preliminary assessment.

5) Subprocessor coordination: if a subprocessor holds implicated data, we will notify you within the same staged windows and provide the subprocessor liaison. Evidence retrieval timelines for subprocessor-hosted artifacts are vendor-dependent and will be called out in the preliminary assessment.

6) Escalation path: Ops primary: Marissa Cole (marissa@redwood.com) > Ben Carter (ben@redwood.com) > PM on-call. Legal escalation: Kimberly Park (kimberly@redwood.com).

Attachments: I re-attached the Draft_DPA_redlines_OptiBank_v1.docx and Export_Checklist.csv for your review. If this aligns with OptiBank's expectations I'll add the exact clause language in track-changes and circulate to Legal.
